newsitem.title: USA: SoCalGas pushes for two-part access rates.
newsitem.headline: SoCalGas pushes for two-part access rates.

text.p: Pacific Enterprise's Southern California Gas Co (SoCalGas) continued Thursday its campaign for a two-part transmission tariff structure for the centralized electricity exchange which the state plans to implement by January 1998.

At a Washington, D.C. technical conference on transmission pricing, SoCalGas said the recently-passed state legislation that would allow electric utilities to recover all fixed costs in base electric rates was a financial burden for customers.

"This is a tax on all consumers," said Dr. Cliff Rochlin, SoCalGas market economist, at the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission conference. "Access to the transmission will benefit generators, so they should share this business cost with consumers."

SoCalGas continues to argued that there is a distinct line betwen the regional and local functions of the transmission system, allowing for access fees based on the portion of the system that is used.
SoCalGas is concerned that a flat transmission rate would be a disadvantage for the smaller California electricity generators that are its customers.
The company presented analysis demonstrating that transmission lines at 500 kilovolts (KV) and above function as regional lines, while those below are used mainly to carry locally generated power.
SoCalGas noted that this is significantly higher than the 230-KV level adopted by the California legislature in its recent electric restructuring bill.
"Having generators pay for their portion of the transmission costs would truly reflect the 'delivered' cost of electricity to the consumer," said Rochlin.

"On the other hand, having the 'postage-stamp' fee provides a strong disincentive to locate new generation near the load, creates a bias in fuel selection and could lead to greater environmental degradation."
